title: Annotatio IV §.VIII: Nicene words — lift the mind to heaven; Lamb of God; little for sanctification
pass_a_gloss: For so the Nicene words have it: Let us not, they say, be humbly intent on the bread and cup set forth, but with mind lifted on high through faith let us consider that on that Sacred Table is set forth the Lamb of God taking away the sins of the world, and truly receiving His precious body and Blood, let us believe these are the symbols of our Resurrection (namely unto eternal life): For therefore also we receive not much but little, that we may acknowledge that we receive not unto satiety but unto sanctification. See the Acts written by Gelasius of Cyzicus and edited by Abraham Scultetus — in these footprints of the Council the easily foremost of all Catholic Fathers and Orthodox Theologians, S. ATHANASIUS, most exactly insists.
pass_b_english: Nicene words (Gelasius of Cyzicus / Scultetus): do not stay humble-eyed on the set bread and cup — by faith see the Lamb of God on that Table, truly receiving His precious body and Blood as symbols of our resurrection unto eternal life.
We take little, not much — not for satiety but for sanctification. Athanasius most exactly follows these Council footprints.
source_text: Sic enim verba Nicænorum habent: Ne, inquiunt, proposito pani & poculo humiliter intenti simus, sed sublatâ in altum mente per fidem consideremus, proponi in S. illa Mensa Agnum Dei tollentem peccata mundi, & pretiosum ejus corpus & Sanguinem verè accipientes, nos credamus, hæc esse nostræ Resurrectionis (puta ad vitam æternam) symbola: Nam ideo etiam non multum, sed parum accipimus, ut agnoscamus, quod non ad satietatem, sed ad sanctificationem, accipiamus. Vid. Acta à Gelasio Cyziceno conscripta & ab Abrahamo Sculteto edita, Concilii vestigiis hisce exactissime insistit Catholicorum Patrum ac Theologorum Orthodoxorum omnium facilè princeps S. ATHANASIUS.
